text:
Charlie Coyle is doing almost everything right for Columbus except the part that shows up in the box score. With him on the ice at five on five, the Blue Jackets get about 57% of the expected goals, the share of chance quality, and are nearly 13 points better than without him. That is one of the best on-ice records on the team.

The goals just won't come. Coyle has two points in his last ten games, against about eight we'd expect at his ice time, and Columbus has scored 12.3 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him out there, among the biggest gaps in the league. His own shooting is at 7.8% against a likely range around 12.7%. Even the highlights tell it: one night a breakaway goal against New Jersey, the next a big Connor Hellebuyck save on him.

At 34, in his second full season in Columbus, he still plays almost 21 minutes, and Evolving-Hockey had him 58th of 401 forwards last season. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds that he's a playmaker first (90th percentile in primary shot assists). When this kind of gap closes, it usually closes in a hurry.
